item.title: Syria aids Saudi Arabia with military advice and training amid Houthi attacks, sources say
item.description:
By Timour Azhari and Feras Dalatey

RIYADH, Nov 6 (Reuters) - Syria is aiding Riyadh with military advice and training as Saudi Arabia comes under attack by Yemen's Houthis, and has sent a limited number of military personnel to the kingdom, two Syrian military sources and a senior US official said.

Saudi Arabia has been locked in worsening hostilities with the Iran-allied Houthis since July, when the Yemen war was reignited by the wider conflict in the Middle East, leading Riyadh to seek both defensive and offensive support from a range of allies.

item.title: Israel opposition touts progress ousting Netanyahu after U-turn on ultra-Orthodox
item.description:
Israel's opposition said Friday it was making headway in its bid to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, as one of its leaders lifted his veto on demands that ultra-Orthodox Jews serve in the military, opening the door to a once improbable alliance with the community.

Neither Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, nor opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot reached a majority in the October 27 election, with Israeli society highly polarised over Netanyahu and worn down by three years of war.

item.title: Paris's Crazy Horse cabaret comes to Dubai -- with less nudity
item.description:
On stage at a luxury hotel, dancers from Paris's iconic Crazy Horse cabaret are rehearsing for their debut performance in Dubai -- but with less nudity than the original version.

The suggestive choreography and subtle lighting of Crazy Horse, a Paris staple since the 1950s, will be on display in Dubai, a city trying to project normality despite the Middle East war.

The women's silhouettes are visible in the half-light, with bare shoulders and legs. But, with local sensibilities in mind, the show will not be topless.

item.title: Iran war spurs crackdown on clerics in tiny Gulf state Bahrain
item.description:
By Timour Azhari

MANAMA, Nov 6 (Reuters) - Shaken by the accuracy of Iran's attacks on Bahrain and support for them among some Bahrainis, authorities in the Gulf island nation have launched a crackdown on Shi'ite Muslim clerics they accuse of fostering allegiance to Tehran at home.

Bahraini officials have framed the move in existential terms, saying Iran seeks to undermine and ultimately topple the leadership of the only Gulf country that is ruled by a Sunni Muslim family but populated mostly by Shi'ites.
